title: SPGR Prioritized Backlog v1
description: The ordered story rollup produced by spgr-prioritize-backlog. Distinct from user-story, which describes exactly one story: this type describes the ORDER over many. Registering it closes the gap the skill itself records ('the prioritized-backlog artifact type is not yet in the schema registry'), and it is the artifact the Linear board projection reads. Entries reference stories by story_id; the per-story user-story artifacts remain the source of truth for story content.

epics.description: The top of the work hierarchy: epic, feature, then story, task, or bug. The board projection uses epic_id to name an issue's parent grouping.

outcome.description: What a user can do when every feature in the epic is done.

features.description: The middle of the hierarchy. A feature is done when every item in it is done and its product check passes on the deployed result. The orchestrator finishes a feature before it starts the next one unless capacity allows both.

outcome.description: What a human sees when the feature is done, in one sentence.

product_check.description: The id of the product check in runs/_product-check.json that proves the outcome.

backlog_order.description: Explicit story_id order. When absent, the order of the backlog array is used.

backlog.description: The ordered entries. Each references one user-story artifact by story_id and carries only the fields the ordering decision and the board projection need.

story_id.description: The item id. A story references a user-story artifact. A task is technical work with no user-facing behavior. A bug references the bug-report artifact that found it.

feature_id.description: The feature this item belongs to. A bug or task found later joins the feature it fixes.
